name: Waseda (Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line))
tagline: Shinjuku in 28 minutes and Shibuya in 29 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥90,000 to ¥100,000.
summary: The station is in Shinjuku City, where the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 37 minutes to Otemachi, 28 minutes to Shinjuku, 29 minutes to Shibuya and 50 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. The station stands 7.7 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 19.0 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 7.7 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 7.5 m to 26.5 m, a difference of 19.0 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 5 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 3 to 5 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is about average for the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 7 clinics and 11 pharmacies. The nearest hospital is 大同病院, about 15 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 国立国際医療センター, about 17 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line).
congestion: The ministry's congestion survey does not publish figures for Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line). It covers the major commuter stretches, and this line is not among them.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥90,000 to ¥100,000 and 1K ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. 1LDK ¥190,000 to ¥200,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is among the highest in the 23 wards.

neighbours.lead: For how little of the area is in the flood projection, Omokagebashi; for lower rent, Waseda (Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line)).
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Waseda (Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line)). It is served by the same lines as Waseda (Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line)). Journey times to the main business districts are much the same. A one-room flat costs about ¥6,000 more at Omokagebashi. On how little of the area is in the flood projection, Omokagebashi comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: For how close the centre is, Waseda; for what it offers families, Waseda (Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line)).
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Waseda (Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line)). Waseda (Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line)) adds the Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line); Waseda adds the Tokyo Metro Tozai Line. Waseda is at least 23 minutes quicker to Otemachi and Tokyo. On what it offers families, though, Waseda (Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line)) comes out ahead.
